{{short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
{{Western name order|Csörnyei Marianna}}
'''Marianna Csörnyei''' (born October 8, 1975, in [[Budapest]]) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] who works as a professor at the [[University of Chicago]]. She does research in [[Real analysis|real analysis]], [[Geometric measure theory|geometric measure theory]], and geometric nonlinear [[functional analysis]]. She proved the equivalence of the [[zero measure]] notions of infinite dimensional [[Banach spaces]].

==Education and career==
Csörnyei received her doctorate from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1999, supervised by György Petruska.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=92512}}</ref> She was a professor at the Mathematics Department of [[University College London]] between 1999 and 2011, and spent the 2009&ndash;2010 academic year at Yale University as visiting professor. Currently, she is at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>Csörnyei's [http://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahmcs/cv.pdf CV] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090902052524/http://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahmcs/cv.pdf |date=2009-09-02 }}</ref>

She is contributing editor of the mathematical journal ''[[Real Analysis Exchange]]''.<ref name=ed>{{cite web | title=Real Analysis Exchange | website=Michigan State University | date=2020-01-03 | url=https://msupress.org/journals/real-analysis-exchange/ | ref={{sfnref | Michigan State University | 2020}} | access-date=2021-02-20}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Csörnyei won a 2002 [[Whitehead Prize]]<ref name="LMS Whitehead Prize 2002">{{cite web | title=List of LMS prize winners | website=London Mathematical Society | url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Whead | access-date=2022-12-06}}</ref> from the [[London Mathematical Society]] and a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]] that same year.
She was also awarded the [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/grants_awards/grants/philip_leverhulme_prizes/|title=Philip Leverhulme Prizes|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100317110739/http://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/grants_awards/grants/philip_leverhulme_prizes/|archivedate=2010-03-17}}</ref> for Mathematics and Statistics in 2008 for her work in geometric measure theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-articles/0811/08111904|title=UCL researchers win Leverhulme Prizes|date=2008-11-19}}</ref>

She won a gold medal in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad|International Mathematics Olympiad]].<ref>[https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=903]</ref>

She was an invited sectional speaker<ref>[http://www.icm2010.org.in/speakers.php List of invited speakers at ICM 2010] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090930192104/http://www.icm2010.org.in/speakers.php |date=2009-09-30 }}</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010.

Csörnyei was selected to deliver the AWM-AMS [[Noether Lecture]] at the 2022 [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]] in [[Seattle, Washington]]. The title of her talk is ''The Kakeya needle problem for rectifiable sets''.<ref name=Noether>{{cite web|title=Emmy Noether Lectures 2022 Lecturer:Marianna Csörnyei|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/noether-lectures/noether-lectures-2022/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

She is included in a deck of playing cards featuring notable women mathematicians published by the [[Association of Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of EvenQuads Deck 1 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#csornyei |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=awm-math.org}}</ref>
